unit.title: Choosing where to invest
unit.description: Safe brokers, fees, neobrokers and robo-advisers: how to compare without falling into traps

texts: A broker with a gift
Pablo
I've found a broker with zero fees and they double your first deposit!
I looked it up on the CNMV and it's not there. But the website is super professional.
What do you tell him?
Grab the bonus, it's free money
Bonuses are the classic bait. Without authorisation, you have no protection at all.
Rule it out: without authorisation, there's nothing to compare
That's it! The first filter is authorisation. Fees come after.
Try it with a little and, if it goes well, put in more
Lots of scams let you win at first so you'll put in more.
A cheap but unauthorised broker is the most expensive one: you could lose everything.
Safety, costs or tax?
Before opening an account, look at three things. Which one does each item belong to?
Safety
Costs
Tax
Authorised by the CNMV or with an EU passport
Check on cnmv.es, not on its website.
Your securities, kept separate from the broker's own assets
They're yours: if the broker goes bust, you should get them back.
FOGAIN covers up to €100,000 per investor
It pays out if a member firm can't return what's yours. It doesn't cover market falls.
Custody fee
What they charge you to hold your securities.
Currency exchange when you buy in dollars
It's usually the most hidden cost.
Inactivity fee
Some charge you if you go months without trading.
Withholds 19 % and reports to the tax office
Spanish brokers do this: your tax return comes almost ready-made.
You declare everything yourself, maybe Modelo 720 too
That's the case with many foreign brokers.
Place the eight criteria.
**Safety first**: authorised and with protection. Then costs and tax convenience, and watch out: compensation schemes in other countries may have lower limits.
Does this protect you, cost you money or is it a tax thing?
Place each criterion

steps.title: The order to choose in
steps.body:
1. **Regulation:** the CNMV or an EU supervisor with a passport.
2. **Protection:** segregated securities and a compensation scheme (FOGAIN, up to €100,000).
3. **Costs:** trading, custody, currency exchange, inactivity.
4. **Products:** does it have the index funds and ETFs you want?
5. **Tax:** a Spanish broker withholds and reports; with a foreign one, you declare everything yourself.
steps.key: First, make sure it's safe and authorised; then, that it's cheap.
steps.tip: Try it: in Market, search for an MSCI World ETF and write down its name.

texts: Cheap or expensive?
You are about to put **€100** into an ETF and the broker charges a **flat €3**. A lot or a little? It depends on what you buy: does it take **less than 1 %** or **1 % or more**?
Less than 1 %
1 % or more
€3 flat on a €10,000 purchase
0.03 %: a bargain.
€3 flat on a €100 purchase
3 %: you'd need to make 3 % just to break even.
0.5 % with no minimum on a €100 purchase (€0.50)
0.5 %. With small amounts, a percentage fee with no minimum usually wins.
€5 flat on a €100 purchase
5 %: you need to make 5 % just to win back the fee.
€2 flat on a €1,000 purchase
0.1 % with a €5 minimum on a €200 purchase
The minimum rules: €5 on €200 is 2.5 %.
Sort the six purchases.

A flat €3 is a bargain on €10,000 (**0.03 %**) and outrageous on €100 (**3 %**). If you put in small amounts each month, look for **low percentage fees or no minimum**; for a few large purchases, a flat fee can work out better.
Hint: €1 for every €100 is 1 %.
Compare the fee with what you're buying
Small things compound
Ana puts in **€100 a month** for 30 years, with the market returning 7 % a year (example). With total costs of 0.2 % a year… or a bit more.
Paying 0.3 % more a year for 30 years: how much does it cost Ana?
About €60
About €6,000
About €60,000
**€6,020** less: €106,703 versus €112,722. A little each year, a lot once compounded.
Set a cost of 1.5 %, like many active bank funds charge.
At 1.5 % a year, costs eat up **€23,630**, more than a fifth. Look at **all** the costs: trading, custody, currency exchange, inactivity and each fund's TER.
A fifth of everything, gone on fees. Without lifting a finger!
Over just a few years you barely notice. Add more years.
Raise the cost and see how much it takes

steps.title: What they charge you
steps.body:
• **Trading:** per trade (flat, percentage or mixed).
• **Custody:** for holding your securities, sometimes monthly or yearly.
• **Currency exchange:** when you buy in another currency. It's usually the **biggest hidden cost**: from 0.1 % to 0.5 % or more per trade.
• **Others:** inactivity, withdrawals, collecting dividends.

And inside every fund or ETF, its **TER**.
steps.key: The cheapest broker is the one that charges you the least, given the way you invest.
steps.tip: Try it: in Market, set up a €100 purchase and look at the simulated fee.

texts: «€0 commission»
Your app charges no commission. But you buy at the best **asking** price and sell at the best **bid**: look at this example order book.
You buy 100 shares and sell them straight away. What do you lose?
Nothing: the commission is €0
The gap between the buying and the selling price
Always 5 %
You buy at 10.00 and could only sell at 9.98: the **spread**, **0.2 %**, gets lost along the way.
Make a big purchase: find a size that pushes your average price up by more than 0.1 %.

The **spread** is a cost even if the app says «€0», and on big orders you also get **slippage**. On top of that, a market maker can pay the broker to send it your orders: that's **payment for order flow** (PFOF).
Your order eats through several prices in the book: you pay more on average.
Look at the gap between buying and selling
How does it make money?
A «commission-free» neobroker makes money in other ways. Which ones grow **the more you trade**?
Earns more if you trade a lot
Earns even if you don't trade
Spread on every trade
Every trade leaves a little behind.
Currency exchange when you buy in dollars
It charges on every purchase in another currency.
Payment for order flow (PFOF)
A market maker pays it for every order it sends over.
Interest on cash it doesn't pay you for
Your idle money earns for it, not for you.
Lending your shares to others
It gets paid to lend them, whether you trade or not.
Monthly premium subscription
You pay it every month, whether you trade or not.
Sort the six income sources.

Knowing where its income comes from tells you **what behaviour it'll encourage**. The EU's MiFIR regulation (2024) **bans PFOF** for retail clients, with an exception in some countries until 30 June 2026.
Ask yourself: does it only get paid when you hit «buy»?
Place each income source
Confetti on every purchase
Pablo
Look at my app: confetti on every purchase and a 12-day trading streak.
This month I've already made 40 trades of about €500. And all for free!
What do you tell him?
Keep it up! If the app rewards you, you're doing it right
The app rewards you for trading, not for winning. The more you trade, the more it earns.
The design pushes you to trade more than your plan needs
That's it. A 20-year plan doesn't need 40 trades a month.
Switch to another app with more rewards
More rewards, more nudges to trade.
With a 0.2 % spread, that's **€480 a year**, even if it says «€0 commission».
An authorised neobroker can be a good option. Just don't let it decide how much you trade.
Try it: open your History and count how many trades you made this month.
What does convenience cost?

An app offers to invest your **€10,000** for you, without you having to think. It charges **0.6 %** a year between management and funds; doing it yourself with index funds, **0.2 %**. Over 30 years and with a 7 % annual market (example), is it worth it?
Over 30 years, how much does the robo-adviser cost you compared with doing it yourself?
About €700
About €7,700
About €30,000
**€7,662**: €71,968 versus €64,306. It's only worth it if it saves you from mistakes that would cost more.
Now set the cost of many active bank funds: 1.5 %.

A robo-adviser usually costs between **0.4 % and 1 %** a year in total: more than doing it yourself (≈ 0.1-0.3 %) and less than many active funds (1.5 % or more). At 1.5 %, **€22,128** goes, nearly a third.
Nearly a third of everything goes on costs.
Move the cost and see the difference
Laura and the 2022 fall
Laura
I don't have time and I never remember to rebalance.
And in 2022 I sold right in the middle of the fall. I still regret it.
Should I get a robo-adviser or build my own index portfolio?
What do you tell her?
Build it yourself: it's cheaper, end of story
Cheaper on paper. But her mistakes cost her more than the fee.
A robo-adviser can be worth it if it saves you from those mistakes
Good: she pays a bit more for automatic discipline. The key: not ditching it during a fall.
Better an active bank fund at 1.8 %
Pricier than both options and, on average, worse than its index.
Careful: a robo-adviser **doesn't remove risk**. If the market falls, your portfolio falls.

steps.title: What a robo-adviser is
steps.body:
An **automated portfolio management** service: you fill in a questionnaire (the **suitability test**), it assigns you a portfolio of index funds based on your profile and takes care of investing and **rebalancing** for you.

In Spain it has to be a firm **authorised by the CNMV**.
steps.key: A robo-adviser automates discipline, but it charges for it and doesn't remove market risk.
steps.tip: Try it: in your Portfolio, check the weight of each asset; a robo-advisor readjusts it on its own.

u33l1-1.prompt: Put the criteria for choosing a broker in order, from the first to the last you should look at.
u33l1-1.explanation: Safety first; price and convenience after.

u33l1-2.prompt: What do you check before opening an account? Select all that apply.
options: Its trading, custody and currency fees
How many followers it has on social media
That it's authorised in the CNMV registers
u33l1-2.explanation: Popularity on social media says nothing about how safe it is.

options: Up to €100,000 if a member firm can't return your money or securities
Everything you invest, with no limit
Losses when the stock market falls
u33l1-4.explanation: It protects you against the firm failing, not against how the market performs.

u33l1-7.prompt: Is it more typical of a Spanish broker or a foreign one?
options: It may require you to file Modelo 720
Your income tax return comes almost ready-made
You have to declare every trade yourself
It withholds 19 % and sends your details to Hacienda
u33l1-7.explanation: Tax convenience also counts when comparing.

u33l1-8.prompt: FOGAIN covers up to ____ € per investor.
u33l1-8.explanation: If a member firm can't return your money or securities.

u33l1-10.prompt: Match each term with its meaning.
u33l1-10.explanation: Four words that help you judge a broker.
right: Scheme that pays out if a firm doesn't return what's yours
Permission to operate in Spain while being authorised in another EU country
Return declaring securities and accounts held abroad
Supervisor of investment services in Spain

u33l2-4.prompt: Match each fee with what it charges for.
u33l2-4.explanation: Look at all of them, not just the one they advertise in big letters.
right: Every time you buy or sell

u33l2-5.prompt: What's usually the biggest hidden cost when buying shares in another currency?
u33l2-5.explanation: From 0.1 % to 0.5 % or more per trade, and sometimes it isn't on the home page.

u33l2-6.prompt: Ana puts in €100 a month. Broker A charges a flat €3 per purchase; broker B, 0.5 % with no minimum. Which one works out cheaper for her?
options: B: it costs her €0.50 per purchase
u33l2-6.explanation: The fee that suits you best depends on the size of your purchases.
feedback: Exactly: €6 a year versus €36. With a one-off purchase of €10,000, though, A would win (€3 versus €50).

u33l2-8.prompt: Paid per trade or every year?
u33l2-8.explanation: Per-trade costs punish trading a lot; annual ones punish holding something expensive.

u33l2-11.prompt: You are going to put €100 a month into an ETF priced in dollars. A broker advertises «€0 commission» in big letters. What do you do before choosing it?
options: I choose the one with the most ads, it must be the most reliable
I also check what it charges for currency exchange and custody
I choose it: €0 can't be beaten
u33l2-11.explanation: The cheapest broker is the one that charges you least for the way you invest: add up all the costs. The tempting one, «€0», fails because it only looks at one fee.
feedback: Advertising says nothing about what they charge you or whether it is authorised.
Good: if you buy in dollars every month, currency exchange can be your biggest cost even if trading is free.
Buying and selling may be free while the cost sits in the currency exchange or custody. The big «€0» says nothing about the small print.

u33l3-1.prompt: What is payment for order flow (PFOF)?
options: What a market maker pays the broker to send it your orders
A fee you pay the broker
u33l3-1.explanation: That's why a broker can advertise €0 trading and still make money from your orders.

u33l3-3.prompt: In what ways can a «commission-free» neobroker make money? Select all that apply.
options: By lending your shares to others
By giving money away to its customers
With the interest on cash it doesn't pay you anything on
u33l3-3.explanation: And also with subscriptions, spreads and products like crypto or CFDs.

u33l3-8.prompt: Payment for order ____ is what a market maker pays the broker to send it your orders.

u33l3-9.prompt: What should you check about a neobroker before anything else?
options: That it's authorised and which compensation scheme protects you
That it gives you more confetti
u33l3-9.explanation: It's a firm like any other: safety first.

u33l3-10.prompt: What do you say to Lumi?
options: Brilliant! The more you trade, the more you learn
Look at how the app makes money and whether those 8 purchases were in your plan
Turn on the crypto alerts too
u33l3-10.explanation: An app can be cheap and at the same time push you to trade too much.
feedback: More trades usually means more costs and more impulsive decisions.
Nice! «Free» is almost never free, and notifications aren't a plan.
lines: I've downloaded a really cool investing app 😍
It's all free and it sends me alerts about shares that are going up. I've made 8 purchases today!

u33l4-1.prompt: Match each way of investing with its description.
u33l4-1.explanation: A robo-adviser is automated discretionary management and, usually, index-based.
right: You choose and buy your own index funds
A manager picks stocks to beat the index
You hand the decisions over to an authorised firm
Automatic index fund portfolio based on a test

u33l4-2.prompt: What does a robo-adviser do after your profile test?
options: It assigns you an index fund portfolio and rebalances it for you
u33l4-2.explanation: It automates the allocation, the contributions and the rebalancing.

u33l4-6.prompt: Is it an advantage of a robo-adviser or of doing it yourself?
options: You don't have to decide which funds to buy
It takes away the temptation to tinker with your portfolio
u33l4-6.explanation: Convenience and discipline versus cost and control.

u33l4-8.prompt: What should you look at before signing up to a robo-adviser? Select all that apply.
options: Which funds it uses and how it rebalances
That it promises the highest return
The total cost: management plus funds
That it's authorised by the CNMV

u33l4-9.prompt: The questionnaire that measures your knowledge, goals and risk tolerance before managing your money is called the ____ test.
u33l4-9.explanation: The EU's MiFID rules require it for advice and portfolio management.

u33l4-10.prompt: What do you say to Lumi?
options: Neither, a bank fund with a manager is better
It depends: if you'll be consistent, doing it yourself is cheaper; if not, the robot helps you not slip up
Robo-adviser, always: robots don't make mistakes
u33l4-10.explanation: There's no single answer: cost versus discipline.
feedback: It's usually the most expensive option and, on average, returns less than its index.
That's it! Compare the extra cost with the mistakes it would save you from.
Robots follow rules, but the market can still fall. And they charge for the service.
lines: Should I get a robo-adviser or do it myself? 🤖
I don't want to be glued to the stock market.
